long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in the industrial community of Greåker, Moan studied mathematics and computer science before founding Cinet, a Nordic networks and servers business. Visma recruited him as chief executive to turn around the financially troubled company. He narrowed its focus to accounting software, then built scale through organic expansion and a sustained acquisition programme.

He co-led the management buyout that took Visma private and oversaw its evolution into a European cloud-software leader. During his tenure, revenue rose from tens of millions of euros to more than a billion. He stepped down as chief executive in 2020 but continues as a director and advises Hg on software investments.

Mr Moan was the CEO of the Norwegian business software company Visma between 1997 and 2020 and took the company private in a management buyout in 2005. By the time he stepped down as CEO, Visma's market value had increased to over €11 billion from less than €50 million at the start of his tenure. He is still Executive Chairman of the Board as of mid-2022.

Mr Moan is also an Industry Advisor to the London-based investment company HG Capital, which owns 54.8% of Visma as of mid-2022. His net worth was estimated at NOK 3.5 billion (approximately €350 million) as of 2021 by the Norwegian website Kapital.no.
